The setup is the segment standard: a web dashboard, AI-generated signals, 12 crypto assets through broker partners, and a US$250 minimum deposit with a demo account included.
The scorecard reflects what the platform publishes, not what its ads promise. We checked the claims against the pages, looked for independent verification, and marked the gaps we found.
whatItClaims: A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
whatWeChecked: The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.
The withdrawal path: steps and any fees the page omits.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Submit your details and activate the account through the verification email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Transfer the US$250 minimum - the sum stays in your trading balance, it is not a fee.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Choose your risk level and trading mode, then use the demo to learn the dashboard.

pros: Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: No named regulator or licence.
Withdrawal fees the page omits.
Support channels not clearly listed.
Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
redFlags: A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.

faqs.a: The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
We rate it 4.1 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$250 minimum is the right size for testing either.
